# Product updates: Sandbox Sidecars, new models, a refreshed dashboard, and more

August brought new model support, faster Function calls, and major improvements across Modal Sandboxes. Here are the highlights.

## 🤖 Day-zero support for Kimi K3, Qwen 3.8, GLM 5.3, and GLM 5.3 Flash

Explore four frontier open-weight models now supported on Modal Auto Endpoints.

All four are supported as Shared Endpoints with token-based pricing, or as Dedicated Endpoints billed by the GPU second.

...

Create a Dedicated Endpoint or use a Shared Endpoint →

## 💸 Improving control over spend

Two updates for better usage control:

- Environment-level budgets are now available for all Team and Enterprise workspaces. Owners and Managers can set a compute-usage budget per Environment and track current-cycle compute usage against it — useful for giving teams their own guardrails without splitting workspaces. Read the docs.
- The usage limits UI got a refresh. Threshold billing and usage limits are now presented with consistent terminology and numbers that add up at a glance, so it's clearer what your limits are and how to adjust them.

## 🌎 Lower pricing for broad region selection

The pricing multiplier for broad region selection has dropped from 1.5x to 1.15x. Broad regions—including the US, EU, and APAC—keep workloads closer to users or data while preserving a larger capacity pool for better availability and faster scheduling.

Read our guide to region selection →

...

We partnered with Moonshot and vLLM to bring day-zero Kimi K3 support to Modal, pairing the 2.8T-parameter multimodal model with a custom-trained DFlash speculator. On agentic workloads, our speculator increases interactivity from 100 to 460 tokens per second and per-GPU throughput from 800,000 to 1.5 million tokens per minute.

highlights:
September 25, 2026· 18 min read

# Best Serverless Platforms for Deploying Agency Swarm Agents in 2026

Agency Swarm deployments can involve dynamic workloads, CPU and GPU inference, API-based model access, and secure code execution at scale, but the framework does not inherently require local GPU inference or sandboxed execution. Recent Agency Swarm releases added local Ollama and open-source model routing through LiteLLM for Agent Swarm CLI requests, alongside hosted provider routes. Selecting the right serverless platform can materially affect scalability, operational overhead, resource access, and responsiveness. For teams building sophisticated AI agents, a purpose-built AI infrastructure platform can make deployment substantially simpler. This guide examines seven serverless platforms for different Agency Swarm deployment patterns in 2026, starting with Modal, the code-first infrastructure used by companies including Substack, Ramp, and Suno.

...

### Understanding Modal's Core AI Infrastructure

Modal's AI infrastructure platform is built on a custom container runtime, scheduler, and filesystem designed for AI workloads. It combines serverless execution with code-defined infrastructure so teams can move from local development to production without separately managing clusters or cloud-specific orchestration layers. Key infrastructure capabilities include:

- 11 priced NVIDIA GPU SKUs: Modal's current pricing lists T4, L4, A10, L40S, A100 40GB, A100 80GB, RTX PRO 6000, H100, H200, B200, and B300.
- CPU and GPU execution: Modal supports CPU-only workloads, GPU-accelerated workloads, and mixed application architectures, which is useful for agent systems where orchestration, tool calls, and model serving have different compute requirements.
- Per-second resource billing: Modal publishes per-second resource pricing for CPU, memory, and GPU compute, supporting usage-based serverless operation.
- Multi-cloud capacity pool: Modal pools capacity across clouds, and its Python SDK supports AWS, GCP, OCI, or automatic cloud selection for supported workloads.
- Fast cold starts: Engineered for fast cold starts and faster feedback loops, with an optimized filesystem that helps containers come online quickly without letting large images slow startup down. Modal's cold-start guidance also describes techniques such as Memory Snapshots for reducing repeated initialization work.
- gVisor-based isolation: Modal's security documentation describes compute jobs as containerized and virtualized using gVisor, adding a strong isolation layer for untrusted execution.

...

Modal supports both CPU and GPU execution, allowing teams to place orchestration, tools, data processing, and inference on compute suited to each component. Modal's current pricing lists 11 NVIDIA GPU SKUs from T4 through B300, giving teams a broad accelerator range for self-hosted inference and other GPU-intensive stages.

...

- ### Can I deploy GPU-accelerated Agency Swarm agents on all serverless platforms?

GPU availability varies by platform and runtime. Modal offers a broad catalog of priced NVIDIA GPUs with per-second billing. AgentCore offers GPU-capable Runtime Instances, Azure Container Apps provides serverless GPU options in eligible configurations, Cloud Run supports GPU-backed services, and Koyeb provides GPU compute options. Microsoft Foundry also provides managed model and agent services, while the compute model depends on the specific agent deployment type. GPU type, region, quota, and billing models differ across platforms.

results.title: Best Cloud Platforms for B200 Access in 2026 | Modal Blog
highlights:
September 2026· 18 min read

# Best Cloud Platforms for B200 Access in 2026

The NVIDIA B200 is a Blackwell-generation GPU. NVIDIA reports 2.3x faster FP16 throughput for HGX B200 versus HGX H100, while workload-level gains vary by precision, model, batch size, software stack, and system configuration (NVIDIA HGX B200). Public B200 access expanded during 2026 across AWS, Google Cloud, Vast.ai, and UpCloud, with availability varying by provider, region, quantity, and purchasing model. This guide evaluates seven providers with publicly documented B200 access as of September 4, 2026, focusing on deployment model, GPU granularity, cluster scale, networking, geography, purchasing flexibility, and infrastructure-management requirements. The list is curated rather than exhaustive: AWS, Google Cloud, Vast.ai, and UpCloud also document B200 access but fall outside this seven-provider comparison. Modal ranks #1 because its serverless AI infrastructure platform combines code-defined deployment, per-second GPU billing, default scale-to-zero behavior, fast cold starts, and an integrated stack for inference, training, batch processing, notebooks, and sandboxed execution.

...

- Serverless infrastructure can reduce operational overhead: Modal lets teams deploy and scale AI workloads without operating Kubernetes clusters for standard Modal workflows. Modal supports SDKs and code-defined infrastructure in Python, TypeScript, and Go, while Modal Sandboxes can run the programming language or runtime required by the workload (SDK documentation).
- Fine-grained billing changes burst-workload economics: Modal meters GPU usage per second and Functions scale to zero by default, aligning compute spend with workload activity (Modal pricing, scaling documentation).
- Cold-start optimization matters for inference: Modal is engineered for fast cold starts and faster feedback loops, with an optimized filesystem that helps containers come online quickly without letting large images slow startup down (Core Platform, cold-start documentation).
- Multi-GPU cluster scale varies by platform: B200 offerings range from VM configurations to large reserved clusters and managed multi-node environments. Modal supports gang-scheduled multi-node clusters with up to 3,200 Gbps InfiniBand networking (multi-node documentation).
- Enterprise security and geography differ by product: Modal has completed a SOC 2 Type II audit and supports HIPAA-compliant workloads on Enterprise plans via a BAA (Modal Security). B200 region coverage differs across providers and can be narrower than each provider's overall cloud footprint.

...

### Key Features

- GPU Memory Snapshotting: GPU Memory Snapshots can restore GPU state and skip initialization work such as CUDA setup, inference-engine initialization, and compilation steps for suitable workloads.
- Per-Second Billing: Modal meters GPU usage per second. Combined with default scale-to-zero behavior, this supports usage-based economics for bursty and variable workloads (Modal pricing, scaling documentation).
- Code-First SDKs: Modal supports SDKs and code-defined infrastructure in Python, TypeScript, and Go. Python provides the full Function authoring workflow, while Sandboxes can execute workloads in any programming language or runtime (SDK documentation).
- Free Compute Credits: Modal's Starter plan includes $30 per month in free compute credits for experimentation and development (Modal pricing).
- Enterprise Security: Modal has completed a SOC 2 Type II audit. Modal supports HIPAA-compliant workloads on Enterprise plans via a BAA (Modal Security, SOC 2 announcement).
- Marketplace Billing: Modal supports procurement through AWS and Google Cloud Marketplaces, including the ability for eligible customers to apply committed cloud spend to Modal usage (Modal pricing, Marketplace announcement).

...

### Serverless Economics

Modal meters GPU compute per second and scales Functions to zero by default when demand disappears. This aligns usage with active compute for bursty inference, parallel experiments, batch jobs, and other variable workloads. Optional warm and buffered container settings provide additional latency controls when retained capacity is useful (Modal pricing, scaling documentation).

...

### Low-Commitment Evaluation

Modal's Starter plan includes $30 per month in free compute credits. Teams can use those credits to prototype B200 workflows, test autoscaling behavior, and evaluate Modal's code-defined development model without a platform subscription fee.

...

- ### Can I use existing cloud committed spend on B200 infrastructure?

Modal supports procurement through AWS and Google Cloud Marketplaces, allowing eligible customers to apply existing cloud spend commitments to Modal usage. Modal's January 2026 announcement described this capability for Enterprise customers, and the current Modal pricing page lists AWS and GCP Marketplace procurement (Marketplace announcement).

highlights:
September 2, 2026 

# New per-Sandbox CPU, memory, and CPU pressure charts

Apps that run Sandboxes now have three additional aggregate metrics charts: per-Sandbox CPU, memory, and CPU pressure. Each chart plots usage against the requested resources, so you can see at a glance whether your Sandboxes are sized appropriately.

When all Sandboxes in an app share the same request, the chart labels it simply as "Request"; when requests vary, it shows the median.
